blueprint.title: AI Cyber Threat Detection & Packet Analyzer
blueprint.overview: Real-time packet inspection engine leveraging deep learning transformers to identify zero-day intrusion signatures, distributed DDoS anomalous payload patterns, and unauthorized network telemetry.

problemStatement.existingProblem: Traditional signature-based firewalls and rule-based Snort systems fail to detect mutated polymorphic zero-day attacks and encrypted payload anomalies.
problemStatement.whyItMatters: Enterprise networks face over 30,000 automated probe attacks daily, risking data exfiltration, ransomware hijacking, and service downtime.
problemStatement.proposedSolution: A dual-engine neural inspection platform combining eBPF kernel packet capture with lightweight ONNX transformer classification to detect anomalies in sub-10ms intervals.
realWorldApplications: Enterprise Perimeter Firewalls & Cloud VPC Protection
Healthcare HIPAA Medical Device Telemetry Defense
Industrial IoT SCADA Network Boundary Monitoring

objectives.mainObjective: Build a production-ready neural intrusion detection pipeline capable of streaming network packet analysis.
specificObjectives: Capture high-throughput network packets using eBPF or libpcap without frame dropping
Extract 42 statistical flow features (entropy, packet inter-arrival time, window size)
Deploy a quantized transformer model with 98.4% F1-score on benchmark PCAP corpora
Build a real-time responsive threat cockpit with automated firewall rule isolation
expectedOutcomes: Sub-15ms packet latency per batch analysis
99%+ precision on DDoS SYN-flood and SQL injection payloads
Exportable defense audit logs compliant with MITRE ATT&CK matrix

feasibility.technicalFeasibility: Highly feasible using modern kernel packet hooks and quantized ONNX runtime bindings.
feasibility.implementationComplexity: Medium-High (requires kernel buffer tuning, vector tokenization, and web sockets).
requiredResources: Promiscuous network interface or virtual TUN/TAP adapter
Python 3.11 with PyTorch/ONNX Runtime & Node.js WebSocket gateway
majorAssumptions: Kernel has eBPF or libpcap privileges enabled
Sufficient CPU allocation for concurrent ring buffer reads
expectedChallenges: Buffer ring overflow under extreme packet saturation (10Gbps burst)
Encrypted TLS payload opacity requiring statistical flow metadata heuristics

architecture.pattern: Reactive Event-Driven Micro-Pipelines with Kernel eBPF Hook
architecture.description: Packets are ingested at the kernel boundary, passed into a lock-free user-space ring buffer, feature-extracted in Python, and streamed to the React Cockpit via WebSockets.

components.role: Feature extraction and quantized transformer classification
Threat event alerting and persistent storage
Interactive visualization, threat filtering, and milestone review

dataFlow: 1. Raw network frame arrives at network interface card (NIC)
2. eBPF filter captures headers and passes payload to ring buffer
4. ONNX model scores threat probability (0.0 to 1.0)
5. If score > 0.85, event logged to DB and broadcast to UI cockpit

learningRoadmap.explanation: Transform raw byte sequences into numerical features: entropy, packet size variance, and inter-arrival timing.

challenges.challenge: Packet Dropping Under High-Volume Traffic Spikes
challenges.impact: Can cause security systems to miss stealthy low-and-slow port scans or brute-force attempts.
challenges.recommendedSolution: Utilize Linux ring buffers (PACKET_MMAP) or eBPF kernel filters to avoid expensive context switching.

challenges.impact: Operators ignore critical alerts if regular TLS traffic triggers excessive false flags.
challenges.recommendedSolution: Incorporate behavioral baseline whitelisting and dynamic sliding-window thresholds rather than static rules.

testingStrategy.overview: Multi-stage test suite including mock packet replaying, fuzz testing, and stress benchmarking.

scenarios.expectedOutcome: Packet safely discarded without crashing ingestion thread

projects.title: ResumeFit AI: Intelligent Resume Grader & Tech Job Matcher
projects.description: ResumeFit AI is an automated resume evaluation and tech role matching platform tailored for early-career developers and students. The application extracts structured text from uploaded PDF resumes, analyzes core competencies, and evaluates formatting, readability, and technical keyword density. Leveraging natural language processing and TF-IDF vector similarity, it benchmarks applicant profiles against curated tech job postings to yield quantified fit scores and actionable improvement advice.

blueprint.title: ResumeFit AI: Intelligent Resume Grader & Tech Job Matcher
blueprint.overview: ResumeFit AI is an automated resume evaluation and tech role matching platform tailored for early-career developers and students. The application extracts structured text from uploaded PDF resumes, analyzes core competencies, and evaluates formatting, readability, and technical keyword density. Leveraging natural language processing and TF-IDF vector similarity, it benchmarks applicant profiles against curated tech job postings to yield quantified fit scores and actionable improvement advice.

problemStatement.existingProblem: Entry-level tech job applicants frequently struggle to navigate automated Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS) because their resumes lack critical industry keywords, clear formatting, or role alignment.
problemStatement.whyItMatters: Over 75% of job applications are filtered out by automated screening software before a recruiter ever reads them, leaving qualified candidates unaware of why they are not securing interviews.
problemStatement.proposedSolution: A user-friendly, transparent web dashboard that parses user resumes, grades them on ATS-readiness across quantifiable metrics, and computes cosine similarity against live tech job profiles to suggest best-fit career paths.
realWorldApplications: University Career Centers providing automated preliminary resume screening for students
Bootcamp and self-taught developers seeking to optimize their profiles for junior software roles
Technical staffing agencies automating initial candidate-to-requisition matching

objectives.mainObjective: Build an end-to-end full-stack web application that parses tech resumes, generates objective grading reports, and matches candidates to appropriate technology roles using standard NLP techniques.
specificObjectives: Implement robust PDF text extraction and sanitation pipelines using Python libraries
Develop keyword extraction and ATS scoring heuristics evaluating structure, grammar, and skill frequency
Build a TF-IDF vectorization and cosine similarity engine to compare resumes against tech job descriptions
Design an interactive, accessible web dashboard using Streamlit to present metrics, scores, and job recommendations
Containerize or deploy the application to a cloud platform for live demonstration
expectedOutcomes: A fully functional web portal capable of parsing PDF resumes within 3 seconds
An automated scorecard offering a grade from 0 to 100 with category breakdowns (skills, impact, formatting)
A ranked top-5 match list of relevant tech roles with similarity percentages and missing keyword suggestions

feasibility.technicalFeasibility: Highly viable for beginners. It avoids resource-heavy deep learning training by utilizing proven, lightweight Natural Language Processing techniques (NLTK, scikit-learn, TF-IDF) and rapid UI prototyping with Streamlit.
feasibility.implementationComplexity: Moderate complexity localized to handling messy unstructured text extracted from non-standard PDF formats, and calibrating keyword scoring algorithms to prevent biased grades.
requiredResources: Free-tier cloud hosting (Streamlit Community Cloud or Render)
Sample dataset of curated tech job descriptions (JSON or CSV)
majorAssumptions: Uploaded resumes are standard text-based PDFs rather than flattened image scans requiring OCR
Job descriptions represent standard industry roles like Frontend Developer, Backend Developer, and Data Analyst
Heuristic rule-based grading combined with vector similarity is sufficient for early-career guidance
expectedChallenges: Handling multi-column PDF layouts that scramble extracted text order
Preventing false keyword positives (e.g., matching 'Java' inside 'JavaScript')
Establishing realistic scoring thresholds that provide constructive rather than discouraging feedback

architecture.description: Streamlit serves as both the reactive user interface and execution runtime. User-uploaded files trigger a linear pipeline passing through text extraction, normalization, scoring heuristics, and vector matching against a local curated dataset.

components.role: File upload widgets, interactive score gauges, missing skill tags, and matched job cards
Extracts raw text from PDF streams, removes formatting noise, and extracts core skills using regular expressions and dictionaries
Computes structural score breakdown and runs vector similarity against job description corpus

dataFlow: Step 1: User uploads a resume (PDF) through the Streamlit web dashboard
Step 2: pdfplumber extracts raw textual content; NLTK cleans and tokenizes strings
Step 3: Rule engine scans for required sections, action verbs, contact information, and tech stacks to compute the Resume Grade (0-100)
Step 4: Vectorizer transforms cleaned resume text and target job postings into TF-IDF vectors
Step 5: Cosine similarity identifies top matching tech job descriptions and highlights missing target skills
Step 6: Dashboard dynamically displays metrics, charts, and ranked job recommendations

challenges.challenge: Non-standard or corrupted PDF text extraction
challenges.impact: Resumes created in graphical design tools (e.g., Canva) can extract as empty strings or jumbled characters.
challenges.recommendedSolution: Implement defensive text checks. If extracted text falls below 50 characters, notify user with a helpful warning that their PDF contains flattened images rather than selectable text.

challenges.challenge: Keyword false positives and substring collision
challenges.impact: Words like 'Go' matching 'Good', or 'C' matching letters inside other words, skewing skill counts.
challenges.recommendedSolution: Use strict word boundary regular expressions (\b[Gg]o\b) and curated case-sensitive checks for short acronyms.

challenges.challenge: Over-optimistic or erratic similarity scores with TF-IDF
challenges.impact: Generic words like 'experience', 'team', or 'software' dominating similarity calculations, resulting in identical scores across all roles.
challenges.recommendedSolution: Incorporate domain-specific custom stop words and set 'min_df' and 'ngram_range=(1, 2)' parameters in TfidfVectorizer to emphasize specific tech phrases.

testingStrategy.overview: A practical testing strategy blending unit tests for parsing and scoring functions with manual exploratory validation using diverse resume templates.

scenarios.scenario: Upload of an unreadable or encrypted PDF
scenarios.expectedOutcome: App catches the exception cleanly and alerts the user to upload a standard text PDF without crashing.

scenarios.scenario: Resume with zero technical skills listed
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Scoring algorithm yields a low technical score and suggests essential foundational keywords rather than failing with division-by-zero.

scenarios.scenario: Matching resume against job descriptions dataset
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Engine successfully returns top 5 unique jobs with similarity scores bounded between 0% and 100% in descending order.
